newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis hails EU pact as victory for Europeans.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis hails EU pact as victory for Europeans.

text.p: French finance minister Jean Arthuis on Sunday hailed the European Union stability pact as a victory for Europeans, sidestepping the perception that Germany had succeeded in tilting the pact more toward automatic fines for countries with hefty fiscal deficits.
Asked whether the pact for ensuring members of single European currency keep their deficits in check was a victory for the French or for German technocrats, Arthuis said, "It was a European victory."

"The Germans wanted automaticity in the application of these fines. France favours a communal discipline, but I fought, practically all night and part of Friday, so that political sovereignty was preserved," Arthuis said in an interview with Europe 1 radio.
"We have rules and we stick to them, because it's in the interest of all, but in last resorts, it's a political decision," Arthuis said.

Under the compromise budget pact clinched in Dublin, leaders agreed that countries would be exempted from penalties for deficits of more than three percent of gross domestic product if their economies shrank by more than two percent in a year.
But any fine would be subject to a political judgment if there was a recession of more than 0.75 percent of GDP. The Germans initially wanted only automatic fines.
